title: Home and household
theme: Cohabitants, chores, a lockout, a broken appliance, a landlord, and moving things in or out.

storylets.title: No key at the door
storylets.note: A subject is locked out until a housemate arrives. Cheap, human and common.

A.desc: an adult at their own door

b1: {A} comes up to the door and pats down both jacket pockets, then the bag.
{A} arrives at the home door and checks every pocket in turn.
{A} reaches the door and turns out a pocket onto the step.

{A} raps on the door, waits, raps again. {n} minutes go by.

storylets.note: A person with a plant. The seed of the quiet category.

storylets.title: The first-of-the-month knock
storylets.note: Rent changes hands at a door. Reads as plain business, never as a verdict.

b1: {B.desc} waits at the door with a tablet under one arm.
{B.desc} stands outside the home door and checks the time.
{B.desc} paces the step in a long coat, tablet in hand.

{A} hands an envelope across. {B.desc} thumbs through it and nods.
{A} passes {B.desc} a folded packet and says a few words.

{B.desc} leaves the doorway, tapping at the tablet.
{B.desc} heads away from the door without a word.

Overheard: {A} says to {B.desc}: "You're the only {B.rel} who comes for it in person."

Overheard: {A} says: "That is all of it this month. Next month, no promises."
Overheard: {A} asks: "Can it wait till the end of the week? Half is here."

storylets.title: A couch on the sidewalk
storylets.note: A drone drops something big. Two people haul it in. Shows who lives with whom, no names.

{B.desc} takes one end of the crate, {A} the other. They count to three.

{B.desc} and {A} work the crate inside and the door slides shut.
